title: Speed up the slowest test binary using newest green CI timings
summary: Read each test binary's "finished in" time from the six shard logs of the newest green main CI run, record the ten slowest in CHANGELOG.md with the run id, then speed up only the single slowest binary's tests without losing coverage, showing its local before/after time. If the cause cannot be fixed without losing coverage, change no code and say so. Audience: maintainers reading CHANGELOG.md.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria check the slowest binary's measured time falls, not just that edits were made.
Times are cited from a named CI run id or a local run, not estimated.
Only the single slowest binary is changed.
Verifier re-runs the one changed binary.
Criterion checks the binary's timing and passing, not file existence.
CHANGELOG entry is written for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: I read crates/athena-cli/tests/ (26 integration binaries, e.g. lifecycle.rs, live.rs, steward.rs), crates/athena-core/tests and crates/athena-data/tests listings, plus xtask/shard-timings.txt; that file holds only estimates (athena-cli --lib 40s and --test lifecycle 40s are its largest), so it is not the real CI data and the real slowest binary must come from CI logs.
The slowest binary is unknown to me; it is likely one of crates/athena-cli/tests/*.rs or the athena-cli lib unit tests, decided by the CI logs.
The producer can read CI logs via GitHub tooling (e.g. gh); the run id is recorded in CHANGELOG.md. Existing CHANGELOG.md has no ten-slowest list yet, so a new entry is added.
Local before/after times come from running only that one binary (cargo test -p <pkg> --test <name>), reported in the CHANGELOG entry; the whole suite is not run.
No governance files change; xtask/shard-timings.txt is not updated, since it is an estimates file maintained by a separate command.
Alternative outcome: if no coverage-preserving speedup exists, only CHANGELOG.md changes and it says so.

acceptance_criteria.text: CHANGELOG.md has a new entry listing ten test binaries, slowest first, each with its 'finished in' seconds, and naming the GitHub run id (newest green main run) they came from.

The CHANGELOG entry states the slowest binary's local time before and after the change, from running only that binary, or states that the cause cannot be fixed without losing coverage and no code changed.
The diff touches test code of only the single slowest binary (plus CHANGELOG.md); no other test binary is modified.

Every test function present in the changed binary before the change still exists afterwards with equivalent assertions (git diff shows no removed #[test] without a replacement and no weakened assertions).
Run cargo test on only the changed binary (cargo test -p <package> --test <name>); it passes, and its reported 'finished in' time is below the 'before' time stated in CHANGELOG.md.

out_of_scope: Running the whole test suite locally
Changing any test binary other than the single slowest
departures: Needs GitHub CI log access and a local run of one binary; the slowest binary is unknown, so cost and time are somewhat above the reference.
